definition_zh: 使大为惊奇；使惊叹；令人惊异
definition_en: to fill someone with great surprise or wonder
core_image: 孩子站在魔术台前目瞪口呆

sceneCN: 这里 amazed 是「使大为惊奇」（第 1 个义项：让人十分意外）；句意为这个魔术让孩子们大为惊奇。

senses.title: To surprise greatly
senses.definition: to fill someone with sudden great surprise
senses.definitionCN: 使人突然感到非常意外
senses.example: The magic trick amazed the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个魔术让孩子们大为惊奇。
senses.why: The old word pictured a person lost as in a maze, so great surprise that stops the mind is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词把人画成在迷宫里迷失，所以「让人一时不知所措的惊讶」是第一义。

senses.title: To fill with wonder
senses.definition: to make someone feel wonder at something great
senses.definitionCN: 使人对宏大之物心生赞叹
senses.example: The view from the hill amazed us.
senses.exampleCN: 山上的景色让我们惊叹。
senses.why: When the cause is something grand rather than puzzling, the surprise rises into wonder.
senses.whyCN: 当引起惊讶的是壮阔之物而不是难解之事，惊讶就升为赞叹。

intro.en: The recorded history of amaze is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 amaze 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old verb meant to bewilder, as if a person were lost.
items.cn: 古动词意为使人迷惑，仿佛人迷失了方向。

items.en: The word was felt to belong with maze, a network of paths.
items.cn: 这个词被认为与 maze「迷宫」相连，那是一片交错的道路。

items.en: Middle English used it for sudden great surprise.
items.cn: 中古英语用它指突然的巨大惊讶。

items.en: English kept the strong sense of stunning the mind.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪保留「震住心神」的强烈意味。

items.en: Today it often describes a trick, a view or a piece of news.
items.cn: 今天它常形容戏法、景色或一则消息。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

definition_zh: 压力；压强；血压；心理压力；催逼；紧迫的负担
definition_en: the force pressing on a surface per unit area; also the feeling of strain, or the act of urging someone to do something
core_image: 一只手掌按在桌面上，桌板把整份重量分散到整个接触面
scene: 潜水员下潜到十米深处，耳膜被水压压得发紧，呼吸也变得费力。 The pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
sceneCN: 这里 pressure 指「单位面积上所受的力」（第 1 个义项：压力、压强）；句意为每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。图中可辨识物件：潜水员、面罩、深度绳、气泡；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Force per unit area
senses.definition: the force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface
senses.definitionCN: 作用在表面上的力除以该表面的面积
senses.example: Pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
senses.exampleCN: 每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。
senses.why: Latin pressura named a pressing, and physics gave the word a precise ratio of force to area.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 pressura 本指「压」，物理学给了这个词「力与面积之比」的精确含义。

senses.title: Pressure in a gas or liquid
senses.definition: the internal pressure of a fluid, measured in pascals or bar
senses.definitionCN: 流体的内部压强，以帕或巴计
senses.example: The gas pressure in the cylinder doubled when it was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 钢瓶受热时，瓶内气体压强翻倍。
senses.why: fluids push outward in all directions, and the word measures that push.
senses.whyCN: 流体会向各个方向推，这个词测的就是这种推力。

senses.title: Blood pressure
senses.definition: the force with which blood presses against the walls of the arteries
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁施加的力
senses.example: His blood pressure rose during the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 他在攀登过程中血压升高。
senses.why: medicine applied the physical word to the body's own plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个物理词用到人体自身的管道上。

senses.title: Psychological strain
senses.definition: the mental strain produced by demands that seem to exceed one's capacity
senses.definitionCN: 由似乎超出承受能力的要求造成的心理紧张
senses.example: The pressure of the final week kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周的压力让她睡不着。
senses.why: something weighing on the mind behaves like a weight on a surface, so the physical word serves feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 压在心头的东西行为像压在表面上的重量，于是物理词也服务感受。

senses.title: Social pressure
senses.definition: the influence of a group that pushes a person toward a particular choice
senses.definitionCN: 群体推动个人做出某种选择的影响
senses.example: Peer pressure made the younger students hide their doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴压力让年纪较小的学生藏起自己的疑虑。
senses.why: a group can press on a person as steadily as a hand on a table.
senses.whyCN: 群体能像按在桌上的手一样，稳稳地压住一个人。

senses.title: The act of urging
senses.definition: the act of repeatedly urging or persuading someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 反复催促或说服某人采取行动的行为
senses.example: The committee applied pressure until the report was released.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不断施压，直到报告被公布。
senses.why: pressing someone is the literal action of the Latin verb, carried into social life.
senses.whyCN: 催促某人正是那个拉丁动词的字面动作进入社会生活。

senses.title: The burden of demands
senses.titleCN: 工作与时间的紧迫负担
senses.definition: the weight of urgent work, deadlines or expectations
senses.definitionCN: 紧急工作、截止期限或期待带来的重负
senses.example: The staff worked under constant pressure during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 旺季期间员工一直在压力下工作。
senses.why: time and tasks can also pile up like a physical load.
senses.whyCN: 时间与任务也会像实物一样堆积起来。

senses.title: A weather system
senses.definition: a region of high or low atmospheric pressure shown on a weather map
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上标出的高压或低压区域
senses.example: A deep low pressure system crossed the coast overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一个深厚的低压系统一夜之间越过海岸。
senses.why: meteorology uses pressure as the variable that organises the whole map.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把气压当作组织整张天气图的变量。

intro.en: Pressure comes through Old French from Latin pressura 'a pressing', a noun from premere 'to press, squeeze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pressure 经古法语来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，它是 premere「压、挤」的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze, hold down'; its past participle pressus lies behind the noun and the English verb press.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤、按住」，其过去分词 pressus 是名词与英语动词 press 的来源。

items.en: Pressura 'a pressing, pressure' was formed from the participle and used for the act and its result.
items.cn: pressura「压、挤压」由分词构成，既指动作也指结果。

items.en: Old French pressure and Latin pressura gave English pressure in the late fourteenth century, first meaning anguish or the act of pressing.
items.cn: 古法语 pressure 与拉丁 pressura 在十四世纪末给出英语 pressure，最初指痛苦或按压的动作。

items.en: The force-per-area sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when experiments on air and fluids needed a precise term.
items.cn: 单位面积受力的物理义从十七世纪有记录，当时对空气与流体的实验需要一个精确术语。

items.en: Blood pressure appears in the eighteenth century, while the figurative senses of urgency and coercion grow from the same idea of something weighing down.
items.cn: 血压的用法出现在十八世纪，而紧迫与催逼的比喻义都从「有东西压下来」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: First English dates approximate: the earliest English use is usually dated to the late fourteenth century and the first physics citation to the seventeenth, though neither date is exact.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：英语最早用法通常定在十四世纪末，最早的物理书证定在十七世纪，但两者都不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same verb that are not the noun; group two holds nouns for force, strain and tension.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词来的形式、却不是这个名词；第二组是表示力、紧张与张力的名词。

entries.definition: The verb means to push down; as a noun it means the printing machines or the news media, not force per area.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为向下按；作名词指印刷机或新闻界，而非单位面积上的力。

entries.definition: To keep the air in a cabin or tank at a chosen pressure; it acts on a space, not on a person's mind.
entries.definitionCN: 让机舱或容器中的空气保持某一压强；作用于空间，不作用于人的心理。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means urgent; as a noun it means an act of ironing or a batch of records.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为紧迫的；作名词指熨烫动作或一批唱片。

entries.definition: Describing someone who is subjected to pressure; it is not the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容承受压力的人；并非名词本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for strain on a person or material; pressure is the force, stress is often the response.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或材料所受紧张的更宽泛词；pressure 偏力，stress 常指反应。

entries.definition: The deformation or damage caused by a load; it describes the effect rather than the pushing force.
entries.definitionCN: 载荷造成的变形或损伤；描述结果，而非推力。

entries.definition: A pulling force along a rope or a nervous stretch; the opposite direction from pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿绳的拉力或神经上的紧绷；方向与压力相反。

entries.definition: A push or pull without reference to area; pressure is force divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 不涉及面积的推或拉；pressure 是力除以面积。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种压下的力展开：物理量、流体内压、血压、心理紧张、群体压力、催逼的动作、紧迫工作的重负，最后是一个天气系统。

definition_en: a large amount of something, to a great degree, and in fixed phrases nearly or hardly

senses.title: A large amount of something
senses.definition: a large amount or quantity of something, especially with uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的大量或许多，尤与不可数名词连用
senses.example: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。
senses.why: The Old English word meant great in size, and size easily becomes amount when the thing counted cannot be divided.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指体积大，而当所计的东西分不开时，体积就很容易变成数量。

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: by a large amount, especially before comparatives or verbs of liking
senses.definitionCN: 大量地，尤用于比较级或表示喜好的动词之前
senses.example: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。
senses.why: Once great size is abstracted, it can measure intensity rather than quantity, so the word starts to mean very or far.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「体积大」被抽象化，它就能衡量强度而非数量，于是这个词开始表示「很」或「远远」。

senses.title: Nearly, in fixed phrases
senses.definition: almost, used in phrases such as much the same or much as
senses.definitionCN: 几乎，用于 much the same 或 much as 一类短语
senses.example: The two maps are much the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。
senses.why: Two things that are much the same have come so close that the remaining difference is tiny, so greatness of degree turns into nearness.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西「大致相同」，说明它们靠得如此近，剩下的差别很小，于是程度之大转成了「接近」。

senses.title: Not a good example of a type, in negative phrases
senses.definition: used in not much of a to say that someone or something is a poor example of a type
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not much of a，表示某人或某物算不上某一类型的好例子
senses.example: He is not much of a cook, but he tries.
senses.exampleCN: 他算不上好厨师，但他肯尝试。
senses.why: If much measures amount, then not much of a thing measures a small amount of that quality, which is a polite way of saying it is poor.
senses.whyCN: 如果 much 衡量的是数量，那么 not much of a thing 就是衡量那种品质的数量很少，这是说它水准不高的委婉方式。

intro.en: Much descends from an Old English adjective for great, and its irregular more and most come from the same root rather than from -er and -est.
intro.cn: much 源自一个表示「大的」的古英语形容词，它的不规则比较级 more 与最高级 most 同出这一词根，而不是靠 -er 与 -est。

items.en: A reconstructed root generally written meg- meant great, and it also produced Latin magnus and Greek megas.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 meg- 的印欧语重构词根意为「大的」，它也产生了拉丁语 magnus 与希腊语 megas。

items.en: Old English mycel meant great or much, and its comparative and superlative were ma and mæst.
items.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的、多的，它的比较级与最高级是 ma 与 mæst。

items.en: Middle English shortened muchel to muche, and the clipped form much became standard.
items.cn: 中古英语把 muchel 缩短为 muche，截短后的 much 成为标准形式。

items.en: By the early modern period much was fixed for amount and degree, while more and most kept the old comparative and superlative.
items.cn: 到近代早期，much 已固定用来表示数量与程度，而 more 与 most 保留了古老的比较级与最高级。

items.en: Modern English much works as determiner, pronoun and adverb, and appears mainly in questions, negatives and fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语的 much 可作限定词、代词和副词，主要出现在疑问句、否定句和固定短语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the irregular family built on the same old root, while the near-meaning group collects other quantity and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词根上的不规则词族，近义组收其他表示数量与程度的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of much, meaning a greater amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的比较级，表示更大的量。

entries.definition: The superlative of much, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的最高级，表示最大的量。

entries.definition: The quality of being much, used in much of a muchness.
entries.definitionCN: 「多」的性质，见于 much of a muchness。

entries.definition: More than is needed or wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 超过所需或所愿的。

entries.definition: A large number of countable things, the counterpart of much.
entries.definitionCN: 大量可数的事物，与 much 相对。

entries.definition: Enough or more than enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 足够或绰绰有余的量。

entries.definition: To a very large degree.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上；非常。

entries.definition: A large amount, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中的大量。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic adjective of size that turned into a measure of amount and then of degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示体积的古老形容词，先变成数量的度量，再变成程度的度量。

normal.en: Old English mycel meant great, and its shortened descendant much kept the idea of a large mass.
normal.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的，缩短后的后代 much 保留了「一大团」的意思。

normal.en: More and most are not formed with -er and -est because they are relics of the old comparative and superlative.
normal.cn: more 与 most 不是用 -er 和 -est 构成的，因为它们是古老比较级与最高级的遗存。

normal.en: Much pairs with uncountable nouns such as water and time, while many pairs with things you can count.
normal.cn: much 与 water、time 这类不可数名词搭配，many 则与可以数的东西搭配。

normal.en: too much, very much and how much are fixed patterns that cover excess, intensity and quantity.
normal.cn: too much、very much 与 how much 是固定说法，分别覆盖过量、强度与数量。

normal.en: not much of a cook means a poor cook, because the phrase measures how little of the quality is present.
normal.cn: not much of a cook 意为算不上好厨师，因为这个说法衡量的是那种品质有多少。

abstract.en: A bowl that is filled past its rim is the picture behind every use of much.
abstract.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗，就是 much 每次使用背后的画面。

abstract.en: Size becomes amount, amount becomes intensity, and intensity becomes nearness: one root, three directions.
abstract.cn: 体积变成数量，数量变成强度，强度变成接近：一条根，三个方向。

abstract.en: English keeps the old irregular more and most as a reminder that this word is older than its grammar.
abstract.cn: 英语保留不规则的 more 与 most，提醒人这个词比它的语法规则更老。

examples.en: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。

examples.en: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
examples.cn: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。

examples.en: The two maps are much the same.
examples.cn: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吃」——马吃东西吃得多，就是许多；记住 much 是许多。

root: 古英语 mycel（大的、多的）经中古英语 muchel 缩短为 much；比较级 more、最高级 most 同出这一词根，一般认为与拉丁语 magnus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a large amount; the senses then divide into a high degree, a nearness in fixed phrases, and the negative phrase that measures a poor example.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是大量；义项由此分出很高的程度、固定短语里的「接近」，以及衡量「算不上好」的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl filled again and again until the grain piles over its rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被反复添满的碗，米粒堆过了碗沿。

branches.en: a bowl filled past its rim
branches.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗

branches.en: a road chosen over a faster one
branches.cn: 放着更快的路不走，偏选这一条

branches.en: two maps laid side by side
branches.cn: 两张并排摊开的地图

branches.en: a kitchen trial that ends in smoke
branches.cn: 一次以浓烟收场的厨房尝试

branches.en: a store of grain that dwarfs the need
branches.cn: 一堆远超所需的粮食

intro.en: The word is an old adjective of size with an irregular comparative family, plus two English suffixes that build a noun and an adverb from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示体积的古老形容词，带着一个不规则比较级词族，另有两个英语后缀从它造出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus, magis and maximus belong to the same old root as much, even though English took the word through Germanic channels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus、magis 与 maximus 和 much 同出一个古老词根，尽管英语是经由日耳曼语渠道得到这个词的。

definition_zh: 老板；上司；负责人；（口语）指挥、摆布
definition_en: the person who employs you or is in charge of you, or to tell people what to do in a pushy way
core_image: 车间里站在图纸旁安排工作的人
scene: 车间一早开工，负责人站在图纸旁，把当天的任务分给每个人。 The boss gave each worker a task for the day.
sceneCN: 这里 boss 是「负责人；上司」（第 1 个义项：管事的雇主或上级）；句意为负责人给每位工人分配了当天的任务。

pos.zh: 动词：指挥；摆布；对……发号施令

derivatives.zh: 由 boss 加 -y 构成，义为「专横的；爱发号施令的」
由 bossy 加 -ness 构成，义为「专横；爱指挥别人」
由 boss 加 -less 构成，义为「没有上司的；无人管理的」

senses.title: The person in charge
senses.definition: the person who employs workers or directs them in a job
senses.definitionCN: 雇用工人或在工作中指挥工人的人
senses.example: My boss asked me to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我的老板让我完成这份报告。
senses.why: The word came from Dutch baas, meaning master, and American workers used it for the man who hired them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自荷兰语 baas，意为「主人」，美国工人用它称呼雇用自己的人。

senses.title: The head of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a team, office or organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导团队、办公室或机构的人
senses.example: She is the boss of the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 她是整个部门的负责人。
senses.why: From the workplace the word spread to any group with a leader, because every group needs someone in charge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从工作场所扩展到任何有领导者的群体，因为每个群体都需要一个管事的人。

senses.title: To order people about
senses.definition: to tell people what to do in a pushy or unfair way
senses.definitionCN: 以强势或不公平的方式叫人做事
senses.example: He likes to boss the younger players around.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢对年轻队员呼来喝去。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, and it kept the pushy tone of someone giving orders without being asked.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，保留了一个人未经邀请就发号施令的强势口气。

intro.en: Boss came into American English from Dutch, and it has moved from master to any kind of leader.
intro.cn: boss 从荷兰语进入美式英语，并从「主人」扩展到任何领导者。

items.en: Dutch baas meant master or head, a word used by tradesmen and sailors.
items.cn: 荷兰语 baas 意为主人或头领，是商人与水手常用的词。

items.en: American English borrowed boss in the nineteenth century, first for the man who hired labour.
items.cn: 美式英语在十九世纪借入 boss，最初指雇用劳工的人。

items.en: From the workshop and the docks the word spread to offices and every kind of employer.
items.cn: 从车间与码头，这个词扩展到办公室与各类雇主。

items.en: In the twentieth century boss became a verb meaning to give orders in a pushy way.
items.cn: 二十世纪 boss 又变成动词，表示以强势方式发号施令。

items.en: Today boss means any person in charge, and the verb still carries a critical tone.
items.cn: 今天 boss 指任何负责人，动词用法仍带批评口气。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape or sound; the near-meaning group collects other leaders at work.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近的词；近义组收工作场合的其他领导者称呼。

entries.definition: The fact of no longer having something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「损失」，读音与 boss 接近。

entries.definition: A small green plant that grows on damp surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苔藓」，拼写与 boss 相近。

entries.definition: A low male singing voice, or a low musical note.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「男低音；低音」，拼写与 boss 相近。

entries.definition: A person who controls a business or part of one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经理」，指管理企业或其一部分的人。

entries.definition: A person or company that pays people to work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇主」，指付钱雇人工作的个人或公司。

entries.definition: The leader of a group or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「首领；长官」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Dutch baas meant master, and American English borrowed boss for the man who hired workers.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 baas 意为主人，美式英语借入 boss 指雇用工人的人。

normal.en: From docks and workshops the word spread to offices and every kind of leader.
normal.cn: 从码头与车间，这个词扩展到办公室与各类领导者。

normal.en: The verb kept the pushy tone, so bossing people around is never a compliment.
normal.cn: 动词保留了强势口气，所以 bossing people around 从不是夸人。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with my, big, around and company.
normal.cn: 它常与 my、big、around、company 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-s-s; the double s keeps the vowel short.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-s-s，双写的 s 让元音保持短促。

abstract.en: See a figure standing by a work plan with a list in hand: that is the boss.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在工作图旁，手里拿着任务清单：那就是 boss。

abstract.en: Give that figure a sharp voice and the word turns into an insult.
abstract.cn: 给这个人配上一副尖利的嗓门，这个词就变成了贬义。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the work plan bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那张工作图把意思带回来。

examples.en: My boss asked me to finish the report.
examples.cn: 我的老板让我完成这份报告。

examples.en: She is the boss of the whole department.
examples.cn: 她是整个部门的负责人。

examples.en: He likes to boss the younger players around.
examples.cn: 他喜欢对年轻队员呼来喝去。

root: boss 来自荷兰语 baas，意为主人或头领，美式英语在十九世纪借入，最初指雇用劳工的人。这个词从车间与码头扩展到办公室和各类雇主，随后又变成动词，表示以强势方式发号施令。今天 boss 指任何负责人，动词用法仍带批评口气。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of boss rest on one picture: a person standing over the work and telling others what to do.
sensesIntro.cn: boss 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个人站在工作上方，吩咐别人怎么做。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure by the work plan handing out tasks
core.cn: 核心意象：站在工作图旁分发任务的人

branches.en: THE EMPLOYER: the person who hires and directs workers is the first sense.
branches.cn: 雇主线：雇用并指挥工人的人是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE LEADER: any head of a group can be called boss.
branches.cn: 领导线：任何群体的头儿都可以叫 boss。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the verb keeps the pushy way of giving orders.
branches.cn: 命令线：动词保留了强势发号施令的方式。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: employer and group leader both mean being in charge.
branches.cn: 负责线：雇主与群体领导者都表示「管事」。

branches.en: THE TONE: the leader and the pushy verb share one voice.
branches.cn: 口气线：领导者与强势动词共享同一种口气。

intro.en: Boss is a base noun and verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: boss 是基础名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin dominus and patronus are recorded words for a master and an employer; they are parallels, not the source of boss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dominus 与 patronus 分别是有记录的「主人」与「雇主」，它们是平行词，不是 boss 的来源。

items.meaning: a master, a person in charge
items.example: Baas is the recorded Dutch source.
items.exampleCN: baas 是有记录的荷兰语来源。

items.example: It forms boss of the company.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 boss of the company。

definition_zh: 课程；过程；航线；一道菜
definition_en: a series of lessons; the way something moves or develops over time; one part of a meal
core_image: 一条从起点流向终点的路
scene: 新学期第一节数学课前，老师把课本发给了大家。 Our maths course will last the whole term.
sceneCN: 这里 course 是「课程」（第 1 个义项：一连串有安排的课）；句意是我们的数学课将持续整个学期。

derivatives.zh: 由 court 加 yard 构成，义为「庭院」
同根名词，义为「球场；法庭；宫廷」
由 dis- 加 course 构成，义为「谈话；论述」

senses.title: A series of lessons on a subject
senses.definition: a planned set of lessons or studies on one subject
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个科目的有计划的课程或学习安排
senses.example: She signed up for a summer swimming course.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名参加了暑期游泳课程。
senses.why: The core image is a path from start to finish, and a course of study is exactly that path walked through lessons.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是起点到终点的路径，而课程正是用一节节课走完的学习之路。

senses.title: The way something develops over time
senses.definition: the natural movement or development of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物自然的运动或发展过程
senses.example: The disease ran its course, and he soon got better.
senses.exampleCN: 病程自然走完，他很快好转了。
senses.why: Because the word first meant running or flowing onward, it fits anything that moves forward over time.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词最初指奔跑或流动向前，所以适合描述随时间推进的过程。

senses.title: A path or line of movement
senses.definition: the direction or line along which something moves
senses.definitionCN: 物体移动所沿的方向或路线
senses.example: The ship changed course to avoid the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 船改变航线以避开风暴。
senses.why: A runner follows a course across a field; a ship follows one across the sea, so the route sense keeps the image.
senses.whyCN: 跑步者沿路径穿过田野，船沿航线穿越大海，所以路线义保留了这一意象。

senses.title: One part of a meal served in order
senses.definition: one of the parts of a meal, served one after another
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序端上的一餐中的一部分
senses.example: For the main course we had fish and rice.
senses.exampleCN: 主菜我们吃了鱼和米饭。
senses.why: Dishes arrive one after another along the meal's path, so each stage is a course.
senses.whyCN: 菜肴沿着这顿饭的路径一道道端上来，所以每一道都叫 a course。

intro.en: Course goes back to a Latin verb that meant to run.
intro.cn: course 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「跑」的动词。

items.en: The Latin verb currere meant to run, giving the noun cursus, a running or course.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 currere 意为奔跑，派生名词 cursus，指奔跑、行程。

items.en: Old French carried it over as cors, meaning a running or an onward path.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 cors，意为奔跑、前行的路径。

items.en: English borrowed cours in the thirteenth century for onward movement.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 cours，指向前的运动。

items.en: Its senses widened to a path of travel, a way of life and a planned study.
items.cn: 词义扩展为行进路线、生活方式和有计划的学习。

items.en: Today course covers lessons, routes, processes and meal stages.
items.cn: 如今 course 覆盖课程、路线、过程和菜式。

note.en: These words share the running root or name paths and lessons.
note.cn: 这些词共享「奔跑」词根，或指路线与课程。

entries.definitionCN: 庭院

entries.definition: a place for games or law; only spelled a bit alike
entries.definitionCN: 球场；法庭（拼写略近）

entries.definition: a long talk or serious writing
entries.definitionCN: 谈话；论述

entries.definition: a long passage, from the same running root
entries.definitionCN: 走廊（同源）

entries.definitionCN: 课；班级

entries.definition: one unit of teaching
entries.definitionCN: 一节课

entries.definition: a way from one place to another

entries.definition: a track or way
entries.definitionCN: 小路；路径

normalIntro.en: The running root and everyday phrases keep course in place.
normalIntro.cn: 「奔跑」词根和日常短语让 course 牢记于心。

normal.en: curs- means run: current, cursor and course all run.
normal.cn: 词根 curs- 意为跑：current、cursor、course 都在跑。

normal.en: of course: things run as expected, so it means surely.
normal.cn: of course：事情照常运转，所以意为当然。

normal.en: A swimming course runs from first lesson to last.
normal.cn: 游泳课程从第一节课跑到最后一节课。

normal.en: Main course arrives after the starter in a meal's run.
normal.cn: 主菜在一餐的进程中介于开胃菜之后。

normal.en: Discourse adds dis-, meaning talk that runs back and forth.
normal.cn: discourse 加 dis-，指来回交流的谈话。

abstract.en: Picture a runner with a flag moving from start line to finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名举着小旗的跑者从起点线奔向终点线。

abstract.en: See a ship's dotted line on the sea map bending to a new direction.
abstract.cn: 看海图上船的虚线弯向新方向。

abstract.en: Plates arrive one by one down the middle of the table; each is a course.
abstract.cn: 盘子沿桌中央一道道端上来，每盘就是一道菜。

examples.en: The new English course begins next Monday.
examples.cn: 新英语课程下周一开始。

examples.en: Of course I will help you with your homework.
examples.cn: 我当然会帮你做作业。

examples.en: Our plane changed course because of the wind.
examples.cn: 因为风，我们的飞机改变了航向。

root: 来自拉丁语 currere（奔跑）的名词 cursus，经古法语 cors 进入英语；核心意象是「向前奔跑的路径」，派生出课程、过程、航线、菜道等义项。

sensesIntro.en: From a running path come lessons, processes, routes and dishes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条奔跑的路径，长出了课程、过程、航线和菜道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that runs from start to end
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从起点跑到终点的路径

branches.en: Planned lessons from start to finish
branches.cn: 从开始到结束的计划课程

branches.en: Something unfolding over time
branches.cn: 随时间展开的过程

branches.en: A line of travel across sea or sky
branches.cn: 跨海越空的航行路线

branches.en: Dishes served one after another
branches.cn: 一道道按序上桌的菜

branches.en: Same path, different walkers
branches.cn: 同一条路径，不同的走法

intro.en: Course belongs to a big Latin family built on running.
intro.cn: course 属于以「奔跑」为基础的庞大拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root currere means to run.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 currere 意为奔跑。

items.meaning: a run out; a short trip

definition_zh: 状况；条件；环境；状态
definition_en: the state something is in, or something that must be true before another thing happens
core_image: 事物此刻所处的样子
scene: 跑道被雨水泡软了，大家都担心赛况。 The track is in poor condition after the heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 condition 是「状况」（第 1 个义项：事物所处的状态）；句意是大雨后跑道状况很差。

derivatives.zh: 由 condition 加 -al 构成，义为「有条件的」
由 un- 加 conditional 构成，义为「无条件的」
由 condition 加 -er 构成，义为「护发素；（空调等的）调节器」

senses.title: The state something is in
senses.definition: the physical state of a person, thing or place
senses.definitionCN: 人或物所处的实际状态
senses.example: The old bike is still in good condition.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧自行车状况仍然良好。
senses.why: Latin condicere means to agree or settle: what has been settled is the present state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 condicere 意为商定：既定之事，即当下的状态。

senses.title: Something that must be agreed first
senses.definition: a rule or fact that must be true before something else can happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生前必须满足的规则或事实
senses.example: He agreed to lend the book on condition that I return it on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他同意借书，条件是我周五归还。
senses.why: Before an agreement settles, its terms are listed as conditions.
senses.whyCN: 协议敲定之前，各项要求便称为条件。

senses.title: The situation around people
senses.definition: the conditions around you, such as weather or work situation
senses.definitionCN: 周围的天气、工作等整体情形
senses.example: The players played well in hot conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 球员们在炎热的天气条件下表现出色。
senses.why: One state widens to the whole set of surrounding states.
senses.whyCN: 单一状态扩大到周围一整圈状态。

senses.title: An illness that lasts a long time
senses.definition: a health problem a person has for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长期伴随某人的健康问题
senses.example: She manages her health condition with care.
senses.exampleCN: 她小心地管理自己的健康问题。
senses.why: A settled state of the body becomes a medical term.
senses.whyCN: 身体的「既定状态」在医学上成了病名。

intro.en: Condition grew from Latin words for agreeing and settling.
intro.cn: condition 生长于拉丁语「商定」的词根。

items.en: Latin dicere meant to say or declare.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dicere 意为说出、宣告。

items.en: Latin condicere meant to agree upon or settle together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 condicere 意为共同商定。

items.en: Latin condicio meant an agreement, then the terms agreed upon.
items.cn: 拉丁语 condicio 指协议，进而指协议的各项条款。

items.en: Old French condicion carried both agreement and state.
items.cn: 古法语 condicion 兼指协议与状态。

items.en: Middle English condicioun kept the terms and the state.
items.cn: 中古英语 condicioun 保留条款与状态两义。

items.en: Modern English condition added living standards and illness uses.
items.cn: 现代英语 condition 又发展出生活水平与疾病用法。

note.en: The first group collects the dic family; the second collects words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收 dic 词族，第二组收近义词。

entries.definition: Dependent on a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有条件的」，与 condition 同根。

entries.definition: With no conditions at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无条件的」，同根反义词。

entries.definition: A statement about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「预言」，与 condition 同根。

entries.definition: Where something is placed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「位置」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The way something is at a moment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「状态」，与 condition 第一义相近。

entries.definition: Something that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「要求；必要条件」。

entries.definition: The general state of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形势；处境」。

normalIntro.en: Remember condition through agreements and states.
normalIntro.cn: 从「商定」与「状态」两个角度记 condition。

normal.en: dicere means to say; conditions are the terms said.
normal.cn: dicere 意为说，条件就是「说定」的条款。

normal.en: prediction shares the same root.
normal.cn: prediction 与 condition 同词根。

normal.en: on condition that introduces the requirement.
normal.cn: on condition that 引出前提条件。

normal.en: in good condition describes a nice state.
normal.cn: in good condition 表示状况良好。

normal.en: Hair conditioner makes hair smooth.
normal.cn: 护发素让头发柔顺。

abstract.en: Picture a used bike checked before buying.
abstract.cn: 想象买车前检查旧车成色。

abstract.en: See two hands shaking over agreed terms.
abstract.cn: 想象握手敲定各项条款。

abstract.en: Feel a runner braving the burning sun.
abstract.cn: 感觉选手顶着烈日奔跑。

examples.en: Check the tyres before the ride; safety depends on their condition.
examples.cn: 骑行前检查轮胎，安全取决于它们的状况。

examples.en: We may go camping on condition that the weather stays fine.
examples.cn: 只要天气保持晴好，我们就可以去露营。

examples.en: Good working conditions help students study better.
examples.cn: 良好的学习条件有助于学生更好地学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯地审」——肯坐下来一地一条认真审，condition 就是商定的条件与状况。

root: 拉丁语 dicere（宣告）→ condicere（共同商定）→ condicio（协议条款）→ 古法语 condicion → 中古英语 condicioun → 现代英语 condition；同族词有 predict（预言）、dictate（听写）、conditional（有条件的）。

sensesIntro.en: Condition runs from settled states to agreed terms, surroundings and long-term illness.
sensesIntro.cn: condition 从既定状态走向约定条款、周围环境与长期疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the settled look of a thing right now
core.cn: 核心意象：事物此刻被「说定」的模样

branches.en: A bike checked before buying
branches.cn: 买前检查的旧自行车

branches.en: Book lent with a return date
branches.cn: 限期归还的借书

branches.en: Players in hot weather
branches.cn: 酷热中的球员

branches.en: A health problem handled with care
branches.cn: 被悉心管理的健康问题

branches.en: Terms agreed before a trip
branches.cn: 出发前商定的条件

intro.en: Condition belongs to the dic family of saying words.
intro.cn: condition 属于表示「言说」的 dic 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root dic means to say or declare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 dic 意为说、宣告。

items.example: The offer is conditional on good marks.
items.exampleCN: 这份承诺以好成绩为条件。

items.meaning: a product or machine that improves a state

items.example: His prediction of the score was right.

items.meaning: to say aloud for others to write

items.example: The room was in a messy state.

definition_zh: 得分；比分；成绩；二十；配乐
definition_en: the number of points in a game, a mark or result, a group of twenty, or music for a film or play
core_image: 球场大屏幕上的比分牌翻到最后一分，观众全部站起来
scene: 终场哨响，球迷们抬头看大屏幕。 The final score was three to two.
sceneCN: 这里 score 是「得分；比分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：最终比分是三比二。

derivatives.zh: 得分者
得分；记分
记分牌
强调；在……下划线

senses.title: Points in a game
senses.definition: the number of points won in a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞赛中赢得的分数
senses.example: He scored twice in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 他在下半场进了两个球。
senses.why: The central modern sense is points in a contest.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是竞赛中的得分。

senses.title: A mark or result
senses.definition: the result of a test or assessment
senses.definitionCN: 考试或评估的结果
senses.example: Her test score improved.
senses.exampleCN: 她的考试成绩提高了。
senses.why: The game sense extends to any measured result.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义延伸到任何被测量的结果。

senses.title: A group of twenty
senses.definition: a set or group of twenty
senses.definitionCN: 由二十个组成的一组
senses.example: A score of people waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 二十个人在外面等候。
senses.why: A tally mark for twenty gave the word this counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 表示二十的刻痕计数赋予该词这一数量义。

senses.title: Music for a film
senses.definition: the music written for a film, play, or show
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、戏剧或演出创作的音乐
senses.example: The film score was written in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的配乐一个月就写好了。
senses.why: A written score is a set of musical marks, like a tally.
senses.whyCN: 乐谱是一组记下的符号，如同刻痕计数。

intro.en: Score comes from Old Norse skor, a notch or tally mark.
intro.cn: score 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕、计数刻线）。

items.en: Skor meant a notch cut into wood.
items.cn: skor 意为刻在木头上的刻痕。

items.en: Score named a tally kept by notches.
items.cn: score 指用刻痕记录的账目。

items.en: A score of twenty became a standard count.
items.cn: 以二十为一组的计数成为标准。

items.en: Score named the points kept in games.
items.cn: score 开始指比赛中记录的分数。

items.en: Score also means written music for a film or play.
items.cn: 现代英语中 score 还指电影或戏剧的配乐。

note.en: Score is compared with similar-looking words and with words for points and marks.
note.cn: 把 score 与形近词以及表示分数与成绩的词作比较。

entries.definition: to frighten someone

entries.definition: a unit of score in a game

entries.definitionCN: 计数；账目

normalIntro.en: Score began as a notch used for counting and now names points and music.
normalIntro.cn: score 起初是计数用的刻痕，现在指得分与配乐。

normal.en: The final score decides the winner.
normal.cn: 最终比分决定胜者。

normal.en: A test score measures a result.
normal.cn: 考试分数衡量结果。

normal.en: A score of people means twenty people.
normal.cn: a score of people 指二十个人。

normal.en: A film score is its music.
normal.cn: film score 是电影配乐。

normal.en: To score is to win a point.
normal.cn: to score 就是得分。

abstract.en: Counting by notches connects twenty, games, and music.
abstract.cn: 刻痕计数把二十、比赛与音乐连接起来。

abstract.en: A score is a record of what has been counted.
abstract.cn: score 是被计数内容的记录。

abstract.en: Music on a page is also a kind of tally of sounds.
abstract.cn: 纸上的音乐也是一种声音的记录。

examples.en: The film score won an award.
examples.cn: 这部电影的配乐获了奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: score 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕），古人用刻痕计数，二十为一组，所以 score 又有「二十」义；比赛记分也来自刻痕计数。

core.en: A record of counting, from notches to points.

branches.en: A counted group of twenty.

items.example: Scoring is easy in this game.

definition_zh: 硬币；铸币；发明（新词）
definition_en: a small flat piece of metal money; to invent a new word or phrase
core_image: 口袋里一枚凉凉的、叮当作响的小圆金属片
scene: 公交车上，妹妹从钱包里摸出一枚圆圆的金属币投进票箱。 She dropped a coin into the fare box.
sceneCN: 这里 coin 是「硬币」（第 1 个义项：金属铸造的钱币）；句意是她把一枚硬币投进了票箱。

senses.title: A flat piece of metal money
senses.definition: a small flat round piece of metal used as money
senses.definitionCN: 用作货币的小圆金属片
senses.example: I found an old coin under the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我在桌子底下发现一枚旧硬币。
senses.why: Metal stamped with a picture holds value like paper, but it rings and never tears.
senses.whyCN: 印有图案的金属像纸一样承载价值，却能叮当作响、永不撕破。

senses.title: To make metal money
senses.definition: to make pieces of metal money in a mint
senses.definitionCN: 在造币厂制造金属货币
senses.example: The mint coins millions every year.
senses.exampleCN: 造币厂每年铸造数百万枚硬币。
senses.why: The thing and the making of it share one word, as the factory gives its name to the action.
senses.whyCN: 物与造物共用一词，工厂的名字也给了动作。

senses.title: To invent a new word or phrase
senses.definition: to make and use a word or phrase for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 首次造出并使用某个词或短语
senses.example: Students coined a funny name for the school rabbit.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们给学校的兔子起了个有趣的新名字。
senses.why: A fresh word is struck like fresh money: new, shining and ready to spend.
senses.whyCN: 新词像新币一样被铸造出来：崭新、闪亮、随时流通。

intro.en: Coin was stamped in the French mint and passed to English with its ring.
intro.cn: coin 在法国造币厂铸成，带着清脆的响声传进英语。

items.en: Latin cuneus meant a wedge, the tool used to stamp metal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cuneus 意为楔子，即打制金属的工具。

items.en: Old French coin named the wedge, the stamp and then the stamped piece.
items.cn: 古法语 coin 既指楔子和印模，也指印出来的钱币。

items.en: Middle English coin settled as the little stamped metal money.
items.cn: 中古英语 coin 定型为小小的印制金属钱币。

items.en: The verb grew: to coin money, and later to coin words.
items.cn: 动词义随之生长：铸造钱币，进而铸造词语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the coin flip for chance decisions.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了抛硬币定夺的用法。

entries.definition: The money used in a country.

abstract.cn: 听硬币落地的清脆银响。

definition_zh: 著名的；出名的；驰名的；（旧）极好的
definition_en: known by very many people, or celebrated for a particular quality
core_image: 景点门口的铜牌上刻着一行金字，游客举着地图纷纷指向它
scene: 游客们举着导览手册，在古城门前排起长队，导游举旗讲解。 The guide pointed to the famous gate built eight hundred years ago.
sceneCN: 这里指「著名的」，对应第 1 个义项：被极多人知晓；句意为导游指向八百年前修建的著名城门。画面要点：导游旗、长队、斑驳的城门。

pos.zh: 著名的；出名的；（旧）极好的

derivatives.zh: 名声（同根名词：被谈论的状态）
声名狼藉的（否定前缀，坏的那半名声）
声名狼藉地（副词化）
有名的（过去分词作形容词，稍书面）
著名地；（口语）非常友好地

senses.title: Known by very many people
senses.definition: known or recognized by very many people
senses.definitionCN: 被极多的人知晓或认得
senses.example: The Great Wall is famous worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 长城闻名世界。
senses.why: To be much spoken of is to be known; the adjective pinned the talk to recognition.
senses.whyCN: 被大量谈论即被知晓；形容词把「谈论」钉在「认得」上。

senses.title: Celebrated for something good
senses.definition: well known and admired for a particular quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因某种品质或成就而广受称道
senses.example: The city is famous for its food.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市以美食闻名。
senses.why: The old Latin word was neutral, but English chose the praising half.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语旧词本是中性的，英语选择了赞美的一半。

senses.title: Excellent, in older use
senses.definition: first-rate, excellent, in older or informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 一流的、极好的，用于旧式或口语
senses.example: We had a famous time at the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上玩得极开心。
senses.why: Enough praise slides from 'talked about' to 'the very best'.
senses.whyCN: 赞美累积，便从「被谈论」滑向「最好」。

intro.en: Famous descends from Latin fama, 'what people say', through its adjective form meaning 'much talked of'.
intro.cn: famous 源自拉丁语 fama（人们所说的），经由意为「被大量谈论的」形容词形式传入。

items.en: Latin fama meant report and public opinion; famosus meant much talked of, whether praised or blamed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fama 意为传闻与舆论；famosus 指被大量谈论，可褒可贬。

items.en: Medieval Latin famosus often carried the sense of renowned, honored.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 famosus 常带「有名望、受尊崇」之义。

items.en: Old French fameus passed the word into England with the positive reading.
items.cn: 古法语 fameus 把带正面色彩的词传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English famous meant celebrated and renowned from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语自十四世纪起即以 famous 表示 celebrated、renowned。

items.en: Modern English fixed famous as purely positive: famous for, world-famous.
items.cn: 现代英语把 famous 固定为纯粹的褒义：famous for、world-famous。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin fam- root or the -ous ending; near-meaning words name degrees and flavors of being known.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fam- 或 -ous 词尾；近义组命名「知名」的不同程度与色彩。

entries.definition: the noun of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词：名声

entries.definition: having a bad reputation
entries.definitionCN: 声名狼藉的；同根反义

entries.definition: wonderful; also, unbelievable
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；也指难以置信的；词源为 fabula「故事」

entries.definition: famous, especially for quality
entries.definitionCN: 有名望的；更书面

entries.definition: known by many, milder than famous
entries.definitionCN: 广为人知的；语气弱于 famous

entries.definition: famous for something bad
entries.definitionCN: 臭名昭著的；贬义

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the adjective of being talked about.
normalIntro.cn: 「被谈论」的形容词，五个抓手。

normal.en: famous is fame plus -ous: full of being talked about.
normal.cn: famous＝fame+-ous：充满「被谈论」。

normal.en: be famous for names the cause, be famous as names the role.
normal.cn: famous for 接原因，famous as 接身份。

normal.en: notorious is famous gone bad: known for the wrong reasons.
normal.cn: notorious 是变坏的 famous：因错事而知名。

normal.en: world-famous is one hyphen that raises the scale.
normal.cn: world-famous 用一个连字符把规模升到全球。

normal.en: famous last words is a joke phrase for overconfident predictions.
normal.cn: famous last words 是反讽语，嘲笑过度自信的预言。

abstract.en: A famous face is one the crowd has already met before the person arrives.
abstract.cn: 著名的面孔，是人在到达之前人群就已见过的脸。

abstract.en: Recognition is a spotlight that follows some names and hunts others.
abstract.cn: 认可是探照灯，追随某些名字，追逐另一些。

abstract.en: To be known for one thing is to have a door with a name plate on it.
abstract.cn: 因一事而闻名，就是拥有一扇挂着名牌的门。

examples.en: The museum is famous for its ancient coins.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆以古钱币闻名。

examples.en: She became famous almost overnight after the film.
examples.cn: 电影上映后她几乎一夜成名。

examples.en: This tea is famous all over the country.
examples.cn: 这种茶闻名全国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费默斯」——费用沉默不了，人人都在谈论你 → 著名的。

root: 拉丁语 fama（传闻、舆论）的形容词 famosus（被大量谈论的）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 fameus 进入英语，词义从可褒可贬收窄为正面声望。同根词 fame、infamous、defame。

sensesIntro.en: From being known by many outward to celebrated praise and an older sense of excellence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「广为人知」扩展到因优而名的称颂与旧义的「极好」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name everyone in the crowd already knows.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中人人早已知道的名字。

branches.en: THE RECOGNITION: known by the many.
branches.cn: 认得：被众人知晓。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: known for something good.
branches.cn: 称颂：因好事而知名。

branches.en: THE SUPERLATIVE: excellent, in older speech.
branches.cn: 最高级：旧用法中的极好。

branches.en: THE LANDMARK: places and dishes known for their fame.
branches.cn: 地标：因名声而知名的地方与菜肴。

branches.en: THE PEAK: the praising reading climbing to 'the very best'.
branches.cn: 顶峰：赞美义攀升至「最好」。

intro.en: Famous is the fam- speaking root wearing the -ous suffix; its family is all about talk and repute.
intro.cn: famous 是 fam-（说）词根戴上 -ous 词尾；词族围绕谈论与声誉。

latinIntro.en: Latin fama and famosus seed the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fama 与 famosus 孕育词族。

definition_zh: 努力；费力的一次尝试；费尽心力做出的成果；集体的协同行动；（物理学）作用力
definition_en: the physical or mental energy used when trying to do something
core_image: 一个人推着装满石头的木车，青筋鼓起，车轮在地面上压出一道痕
scene: 山路太陡，几个人一起推同一辆货车，车轮才勉强往前走。 Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 指「为达成一件事而付出的体力或脑力」（第 1 个义项：付出力气去做）；句意为他们合力只把车推动了几米就不得不停下。图中可辨识物件：木车、陡坡、被压出的车辙、几双用力的腿。

pos.zh: 努力；尝试；费力得到的成果；协同行动

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「需要使力气的」
在形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「费力的」转为「以费力方式」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「看起来不费力气」
在否定式形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「不费力的」转为「毫不费力地」
在否定式形容词后加名词后缀构成，语义由「不费力」转为「不费力这一特质」

senses.title: Energy spent on a task
senses.titleCN: 为做成一件事付出的力气
senses.definition: the physical or mental energy that someone uses in trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人为做成某件事而投入的体力或脑力
senses.example: Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合力只把车推动了大约几米，就不得不停下休息。
senses.why: the word descends from a Latin verb meaning to strengthen, so the first sense is simply the strength that a task draws out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一个意为「使有力」的拉丁动词，所以第一个义项就是一件事从人身上抽出的那股力。

senses.title: A single attempt
senses.definition: one act of trying to do something, viewed as a countable attempt
senses.definitionCN: 试着做某事的一次行动，可以按次计数
senses.example: He made three efforts to lift the lid before asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着揭开盖子三次，才去求助。
senses.why: once energy is spent it can be counted as a try, so the noun shifts from the fuel to the event that burns it.
senses.whyCN: 力气一旦花出去，就可以说成「一次尝试」，于是名词从燃料转向烧掉燃料的那件事。

senses.title: A piece of work produced
senses.definition: a result or piece of work judged by how much care and labour went into it
senses.definitionCN: 按投入的心血与劳动来评价的成果或作品
senses.example: Her essay was a serious effort, even if the argument faltered.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章是一份认真写就的成果，尽管论证有些摇晃。
senses.why: we praise a thing by naming the labour inside it, so the word can stand for the product rather than the process.
senses.whyCN: 人们通过点出其中所含的劳动来称赞一件东西，于是这个词可以用产物代替过程。

senses.title: Organized collective action
senses.definition: a coordinated campaign in which many people work toward one public aim
senses.definitionCN: 许多人朝同一个公共目标协作推进的行动
senses.example: The relief effort reached the valley two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援行动抵达了山谷。
senses.why: when many people spend energy on one aim, the countable noun becomes the whole campaign rather than any single exertion.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人把力气投向一个目标时，这个可数名词指的就是整场行动，而不是任何单次用力。

senses.title: Force applied in a machine
senses.definition: in mechanics, the force applied to a machine or load, as opposed to the resistance it moves
senses.definitionCN: 力学中施加于机械或负载的力，与它所推动的阻力相对
senses.example: A longer lever increases the effect of the effort on the load.
senses.exampleCN: 较长的杠杆会增大作用力对负载的效果。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the plain meaning exactly: the force a worker puts in, measured against what the machine must move.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义保留了最朴素的意思：人使出的那股力，与机器要移动的东西相对而量。

senses.title: Degree of strain involved
senses.definition: the amount of strain a task demands, considered as a property of the task
senses.definitionCN: 任务所要求的紧张程度，作为任务本身的属性来看
senses.example: The climb costs little effort if you start early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果早点出发，这段爬坡并不费多少力气。
senses.why: instead of the energy itself, the word can name the quantity of it that a job requires, which is why one asks how much effort a task takes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指力气本身，而指一件事所需的力气分量，所以人们会问一项任务要花多少努力。

senses.title: National mobilization
senses.definition: the total organized activity of a country or a large body in wartime or emergency
senses.definitionCN: 战时或紧急状态下，一国或一个大型机构投入的全部组织性活动
senses.example: The war effort drew factories, farms and railways into one plan.
senses.exampleCN: 战时动员把工厂、农场与铁路都纳入一个计划。
senses.why: this is the collective sense enlarged to the scale of a whole society, where every exertion feeds a single campaign.
senses.whyCN: 这是集体义被放大到整个社会的规模：每一份力气都汇入同一场行动。

senses.title: An attempt judged kindly
senses.titleCN: 值得称许的一次尝试（即使未成）
senses.definition: an attempt that is praised for the honesty of the trying even though it falls short
senses.definitionCN: 即便未达到目标，也因尝试本身认真而受到赞许的一次努力
senses.example: The team lost, but it was a brave effort by every player.
senses.exampleCN: 球队输了，但每位队员的这次努力都很勇敢。
senses.why: because effort measures what was given rather than what was gained, the word becomes a way of honouring a failure.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词量的是付出而非所得，它就成了给失败留体面的一种说法。

intro.en: Effort comes through Old French esforz from the verb esforcier 'to force, exert', which rests on a Vulgar Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare, from Latin fortis 'strong'. The deeper origin of fortis is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 esforz 来自动词 esforcier「用力、使力」，后者基于一个被重构为 exfortiare 的俗拉丁动词，其词根为拉丁 fortis「强壮」。fortis 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, mighty, firm'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link proposed to a root for 'height' or 'mountain' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮、有力、坚固」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「高度」或「山」的词根相联系的看法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: A spoken-Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare 'to put forth strength' carried the root into the everyday speech of the late empire; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 一个被重构为 exfortiare 的口语拉丁动词「使出力气」，把词根带入帝国晚期日常口语；这一形式属重构，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French esforcier 'to force, strive, exert oneself' produced the noun esforz, which named both the strain and the try.
items.cn: 古法语 esforcier「用力、奋力、施展」产生名词 esforz，兼指那份紧张与那次尝试。

items.en: Middle English took the noun as effort in the fourteenth century, still close to the sense of a strong exertion of the will.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪把这个名词吸收为 effort，仍贴近「意志强力施展」的意思。

items.en: From the nineteenth century mechanics used effort for the applied force in a simple machine, set against the load it moves.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，力学用这个词指简单机械中施加的力，与被移动的负载相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of fortis and the exact spoken form): any Indo-European form offered for fortis is a reconstruction, and the earliest noun use has no securely dated citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（fortis 的更深来源与那个口语形式的确切面貌）：凡为 fortis 给出的印欧语形式均为重构形式；这个名词最早用法也没有确切年代的出处。

note.en: Group one collects words that look like effort but come from other roots; group two collects near neighbours that measure exertion differently.
note.cn: 第一组是形近而异源的词；第二组是语义相近、但衡量「付出」方式不同的词。

entries.definition: Its negation: work done without visible strain, so the strain is precisely what has vanished.
entries.definitionCN: 该词的否定形式：不显费力的工作，消失的正是那份紧张。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus fortis: what strengthens someone, hence ease and consolation, not exertion.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 fortis 构成：使人强健之物，因此指舒适与安慰，而非付出。

entries.definition: Fortis 'strong' plus facere 'to make': to make strong, as a wall or a body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 fortis「强壮」加 facere「做」构成：使变强，如城墙或身体。

entries.definition: Strength of mind under pain or pressure; it names the capacity rather than its spending.
entries.definitionCN: 痛苦或压力下心志的坚强；指那份能力，而不是它的耗费。

entries.definition: From for- 'outside' plus a Germanic root for a fine: to lose something as a penalty, with no link to strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 for-「在外」加一个表示罚金的日耳曼词根构成：作为惩罚而失去某物，与「强壮」无关。

entries.definition: The activity of labouring, named by what is done rather than by the strain it costs.
entries.definitionCN: 指劳动这项活动，以「做了什么」命名，而不以耗费多少力气命名。

entries.definition: A formal word for strong physical or mental strain; effort is its everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示强烈体力或脑力紧张的正式词；effort 是它日常的对应说法。

entries.definition: A try at something, with the outcome unknown; it says nothing about how much energy was spent.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的尝试，结果未知；不含花费了多少力气之意。

entries.definition: A sustained, purposeful effort, often on something public or grand; it carries a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 持久的、有目的的付出，多用于公共或宏大的事；语气正式。

entries.definition: Hard physical work, especially of a manual or repetitive kind; it stresses the grind.
entries.definitionCN: 艰苦的体力劳动，尤指手工或重复性工作；强调辛苦本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin fortis 'strong', so effort is strength brought out and spent.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此这个词就是被使出来、被花掉的力气。

normal.en: The family runs effort, effortless, effortful, effortlessly, effortlessness.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、肯定与否定两个形容词、副词与抽象名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spending: make an effort, put effort into, spare no effort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这份耗费：作出努力、投入心力、不遗余力。

normal.en: The technical use appears in the lever: effort acts on one arm, the load on the other.
normal.cn: 技术义出现在杠杆里：施力作用于一端，负载作用于另一端。

normal.en: Relatives outside the word still carry the same root: fortify, fortitude, comfort.
normal.cn: 词外的同族词仍然带着同一词根：加固、坚毅、安慰。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing water out of a cloth until the drops stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把布里的水拧出来，直到不再滴。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled taut between two posts, humming with the strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子在两根柱子之间被拉紧，绷得发出声。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burned down to a stub because it was kept lit all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛因为整夜点着，只剩下一小截。

examples.en: It took a full day of effort to clear the blocked channel.
examples.cn: 清理这条堵塞的水道花了整整一天的力气。

examples.en: The rescue effort involved boats, dogs and six villages.
examples.cn: 这次救援行动动用了船只、犬只与六个村庄的人手。

examples.en: A lever lets a small effort lift a heavy load.
examples.cn: 杠杆使小小的作用力能抬起沉重的负载。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一夫」推车——一个人使出全身力气推车 → 努力、费力

root: 古法语 esforz「力气、奋力」→ 俗拉丁重构形式 exfortiare「使出力气」→ 拉丁 fortis「强壮、有力」；fortis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: strength is drawn out of a body, counted as a try, then read into the thing made, into the group that shares it, into the machine that measures it, into the size of the demand, into a whole nation's campaign and finally into the praise given to a losing attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：力气从身体里被抽出，先被数成一次尝试，再被读进做出的东西、共担的群体、量它的机械、需求的大小、举国的动员，最后读进给失败尝试的那份称许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body braced against a loaded cart, strength visibly leaving it and entering the work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体抵着装满货物的车，力气看得见地从身体里流出，进入那件活里。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY AND ITS SIZE: energy itself, and the amount of it a task calls for.

intro.en: Effort is a noun taken whole from Old French, so it has no live prefixes for English speakers; what grows from it are suffixes and a root that still builds other words.

senses.title: A person who practises law
senses.definition: someone whose profession is law, whether advising or representing
senses.definitionCN: 以法律为职业的人，提供咨询或代理皆可
senses.example: The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.
senses.exampleCN: 律师标出了三条可能让租客多花钱的条款。
senses.why: The word is built from law plus an agent ending, so it names the profession by its subject matter rather than by a court role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「法律」加施事后缀构成，所以它按业务内容命名职业，而不是按法庭角色命名。

senses.title: An adviser working outside court
senses.definition: a legal adviser whose work is done in an office rather than in court
senses.definitionCN: 主要在办公室而非法庭上工作的法律顾问
senses.example: Our lawyer reviewed the insurance policy line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的律师逐行审阅了保险条款。
senses.why: Most legal work is paperwork and advice, so the everyday word usually points to the desk rather than to the dock.
senses.whyCN: 多数法律工作是文书与咨询，所以这个日常词通常指向办公桌，而不是法庭上的席位。

senses.title: An advocate who speaks in court
senses.definition: a legal practitioner who argues a case before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前为案件辩论的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer spoke for forty minutes without looking at her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师讲了四十分钟，全程没看笔记。
senses.why: The same noun serves the courtroom because advocacy is the part of the profession the public sees and remembers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也用于法庭，因为辩护是公众看得见、记得住的那部分工作。

senses.title: The profession as a group
senses.definition: lawyers considered collectively, often in commentary or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的律师，常用于评论或批评
senses.example: The lawyers for both sides met privately before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，双方的律师私下见了面。
senses.why: A countable noun used in the plural can stand for a whole trade, which is why the word appears in sentences about the profession as a force.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用复数时可以代表整个行业，所以这个词会出现在把律师界当作一股力量的句子里。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a practitioner who works in a particular field of law
senses.definitionCN: 在某一法律领域执业的律师
senses.example: They consulted a patent lawyer before filing the design.
senses.exampleCN: 申请外观设计前，他们咨询了专利律师。
senses.why: Modern law divides into fields, and the word attaches to the field as a modifier, turning the general noun into a specialism.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律分成许多领域，这个词作为修饰成分附着在领域上，就把通称变成了专业分工。

senses.title: The person who drafts the papers
senses.definition: the practitioner who prepares contracts, deeds and other documents
senses.definitionCN: 准备合同、契据等文书的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer drafted the deed so that either heir could sell.
senses.exampleCN: 律师起草的契据让两位继承人都能出售。
senses.why: Drafting is invisible in court but decisive in outcome, so the word also covers the quiet work behind a signature.
senses.whyCN: 起草在法庭上看不见，却决定结果，所以这个词也覆盖签名背后那份安静的工作。

senses.title: A sea lawyer
senses.titleCN: 好抬杠的水手；爱抠规则的人
senses.definition: an argumentative sailor, or anyone who quibbles about rules without authority
senses.definitionCN: 爱争辩的水手，或任何没有职权却抠规则字眼的人
senses.example: The cook was a sea lawyer who could quote every regulation but never follow one.
senses.exampleCN: 那个厨子是个爱抬杠的水手，条条规则都能背，却一条也不照做。
senses.why: Sailors with time on their hands argued about regulations, and the fixed phrase transferred that habit to land as a mild insult.
senses.whyCN: 水手闲来无事就争论规章，这个固定说法把这种习气带上岸，成了轻度的讥称。

senses.title: A clever arguer on technicalities
senses.definition: a person who argues by exploiting fine points rather than by merit
senses.definitionCN: 靠抠细枝末节而非讲道理取胜的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a lawyer to win that argument, only patient.
senses.exampleCN: 赢那场争论不必是律师，只需要有耐心。
senses.why: Because the trade is associated with precise wording, the noun can describe anyone who fights with clauses instead of facts.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个行业与精确措辞联系在一起，这个名词便能描述任何用条款而非事实来争论的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is an English compound of law and an agent ending. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', while the ending is a variant of -ier from Old French, ultimately Latin -arius.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语用 law 加施事后缀构成的复合词。law 来自古诺斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，词尾则是古法语 -ier 的变体，最终上溯拉丁 -arius。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down, a layer or a fixed order; its plural log named customary law in the Norse-speaking world.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下的东西、一层或既定秩序；其复数 lǫg 在诺斯语世界指习惯法。

items.en: English borrowed lagu for law, covering both the body of rules and the custom of a district, a word that displaced the older native term.
items.cn: 英语借入 lagu 表示法律，既指整套规则，也指一地的习惯，并取代了更早的本族词。

items.en: The Latin agent suffix -arius, through Old French -ier, formed words for people concerned with a thing, and it is the source of the ending here.
items.cn: 拉丁施事后缀 -arius 经古法语 -ier，构成「与某物打交道的人」，这里这个词尾正源于此。

items.en: Middle English had lawier beside lawyer; the spelling with y won out, and the word settled on the profession as a whole.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lawier 与 lawyer 并存，带 y 的拼法最终胜出，这个词也固定指整个职业。

items.en: Modern English uses lawyer as the neutral everyday term, while attorney carries American formality and counsel carries courtroom colour.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lawyer 当作中性日常说法，attorney 带美国式的正式感，counsel 则带法庭色彩。

note.en: Group one separates the base word and the derived family from two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the plain word against the formal and regional titles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词与派生词族，同两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把日常通称与正式称谓、地区称谓作对照。

entries.definition: The rules themselves; lawyer is the person whose trade is those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身；lawyer 是以这些规则为业的人。

entries.definition: Resembling a lawyer or the manner of legal argument, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 像律师的、像法律辩论腔调的，不是指人。

entries.definition: The practice or craft of being a lawyer, viewed as work rather than as a role.
entries.definitionCN: 指律师的实务与手艺，看作工作而非角色。

entries.definition: One who saws wood, from saw plus the same agent ending; the shape matches but the base is a tool, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 锯木的人，由 saw 加同一个施事后缀构成；外形相似，基础词却是工具而非法律。

entries.definition: A law-enforcement officer, built from law plus man; it names an officer, not a legal adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 执法官员，由 law 加 man 构成；它指警官，不是法律顾问。

entries.definition: The formal American word for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: A legal adviser or the advocates in a case, often a mass noun with a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 法律顾问或案中的辩护人，常作不可数名词，语气正式。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer who advises and prepares documents rather than pleading in higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指提供咨询、准备文书而不在高等法院辩论的律师。

entries.definition: In Britain, a lawyer specially qualified to plead in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指有资格在高等法院出庭辩论的律师。

entries.definition: A person who pleads for another, in law or in a cause; the word stresses speaking for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人或某项事业辩护的人；这个词强调替人发声。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Norse source of law and the real agent ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 law 真实的诺斯语来源，以及真实的施事后缀。

normal.en: Law is 'what is laid down', and a lawyer is the person who works with what is laid down.
normal.cn: law 是「被放下的东西」，lawyer 就是与这些既定规则打交道的人。

normal.en: The -yer ending is a spelling of the agent ending that also built sawyer, a woodcutter.
normal.cn: -yer 是施事后缀的一种拼法，它也构成了 sawyer，即锯木人。

normal.en: Sawyer looks like lawyer but starts from a tool, so the two words share an ending and nothing else.
normal.cn: sawyer 形似 lawyer，却从工具起头，两词只共享词尾，别无其他。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the settings: a practising lawyer, a defence lawyer, a company lawyer.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：执业律师、辩护律师、公司法务。

normal.en: The plain word sits between attorney and counsel: less formal than one, less courtroom-bound than the other.
normal.cn: 这个通称夹在 attorney 与 counsel 之间：比前者随意，比后者少些法庭气。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of folders with coloured tabs, one tab for each field of law.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗，每个法律领域一个标签。

abstract.en: Picture a person reading a contract with a red pen, circling what could cost money.

examples.en: A good lawyer tells you what not to sign, not only what to sign.
examples.cn: 好律师会告诉你什么别签，而不只是什么该签。

examples.en: The company keeps two lawyers in house and hires outside counsel for big cases.
examples.cn: 公司内部留了两名律师，大案子再请外部顾问。

examples.en: He joked that every family needs a doctor, a lawyer and a locksmith.
examples.cn: 他开玩笑说，每个家庭都需要一个医生、一个律师和一个锁匠。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the profession as a whole, through office advice, courtroom advocacy, the trade seen as a group, specialist practice and document drafting, to the sea lawyer and the mere quibbler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整个职业开始，经办公室咨询、出庭辩护、作为群体的律师界、专长执业与文书起草，最后到「好抬杠的水手」和只会钻字眼的争辩者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tabbed files on a desk, one clause circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上一摞贴标签的卷宗，其中一条被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE TRADE: the agent ending turns the rules into a person whose work they are.
branches.cn: 职业：施事后缀把「规则」变成以此为业的人。

branches.en: THE DESK: most of the work is reading, warning and drafting outside court.
branches.cn: 办公桌：多数工作是在法庭之外阅读、提醒与起草。

branches.en: THE VOICE AND THE BODY: the same noun covers the speaker in court and the profession as a collective force.
branches.cn: 声音与群体：同一个名词既指庭上发言者，也指作为一股力量的整个行业。

branches.en: THE NARROWING: fields and paperwork split the general word into specialisms and quiet desk work.
branches.cn: 细分：领域与文书把这个通称分成专业分工与安静的案头工作。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the trade's prestige also produces mock titles for quibblers and technical arguers.
branches.cn: 讥称：这个行业的声望也造出了挖苦人的称号，指爱抬杠与钻字眼的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is a home-built English compound: a Norse-derived noun plus a French-derived agent ending.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语本土拼装的复合词：一个源自诺斯语的名词，加一个源自法语的施事后缀。

latinIntro.en: The ending is Latin -arius, which reached English through Old French -ier; the noun law itself is not Latin but Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾是拉丁 -arius，经古法语 -ier 进入英语；而名词 law 本身并非拉丁语，而是诺斯语。

senses.title: Stuff used to build or make
senses.titleCN: 用来建造或制作的材料
senses.definition: the substance out of which something is made or built
senses.definitionCN: 用来制造或建造某物的物质
senses.example: Bricks and timber were the material of the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 砖与木料是这座老桥的材料。
senses.why: Late Latin materialis was simply the adjective of materia 'stuff', so the noun kept the plain sense of the stuff itself.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁 materialis 就是 materia「材料」的形容词，名词义因此保留了「料本身」这层直白意思。

senses.title: Cloth for sewing
senses.definition: fabric used for making clothes or furnishings
senses.definitionCN: 用来做衣服或家居用品的布料
senses.example: The tailor spread the material and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把布料铺开，沿粉线裁剪。
senses.why: cloth was the material a household handled most often, so the word narrowed to fabric in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 布料是家庭最常打交道的材料，于是这个词在日常口语中收窄为「织物」。

senses.title: Facts and sources for a work
senses.definition: information, notes or sources used for writing, research or a report
senses.definitionCN: 用于写作、研究或报道的信息、笔记与来源
senses.example: The reporter gathered material for the story over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 记者用三周时间为这篇报道收集素材。
senses.why: what clay is to a pot, notes are to an article, so the same word covers the raw stuff of a text.
senses.whyCN: 黏土之于陶罐，正如笔记之于文章，于是同一个词也指文本的原料。

senses.title: Supplies and equipment
senses.definition: the things needed for a particular activity, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所需的物品，通常用复数
senses.example: The laboratory ordered its materials for the autumn term.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室订购了秋季学期要用的用品。
senses.why: in the plural the word counts separate items rather than an uncountable stuff, a shift English makes freely with substances.
senses.whyCN: 复数把不可数的「料」转成一件件可数的东西，英语对物质名词常有这种转换。

senses.title: Physical rather than spiritual
senses.titleCN: 物质层面的，与精神相对
senses.definition: belonging to the physical world rather than to thought or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理世界，而非思想或精神世界
senses.example: The material world still obeys physical law.
senses.exampleCN: 物质世界依然服从物理规律。
senses.why: the adjective kept the old opposition of stuff to spirit, so it describes whatever can be touched.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「材料对精神」的古老对举，因此描述一切摸得着的东西。

senses.title: Important to a decision
senses.definition: significant enough to affect a decision, a contract or a judgment
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以影响决定、合同或判断的
senses.example: The delay was material to the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对合同条款有实质影响。
senses.why: law and accounting borrowed the word because a fact with real stuff in it can change an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 法律与会计借用这个词，因为有实体内容的事实才足以改变结果。

senses.title: Concerned with wealth
senses.definition: interested in money and possessions rather than in higher aims
senses.definitionCN: 看重金钱与财物而非更高追求
senses.example: They chased material gain and ignored the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们追逐物质利益，无视造成的损害。
senses.why: if the material world is what can be touched, then gain in that world is money and goods.
senses.whyCN: 既然物质世界就是摸得着的那一面，那么那一面的收获自然就是钱与物。

senses.title: A person suited to a role
senses.definition: a person considered as suitable raw stuff for a particular post or task
senses.definitionCN: 被看作适合某项职位或任务的「生料」
senses.example: She is good material for the debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是辩论队的好苗子。
senses.why: a person is treated as raw stuff to be shaped by training, which keeps the oldest sense of material alive in a comic way.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成可被训练塑造的生料，这以略带戏谑的方式保留了 material 最古老的意思。

intro.en: Material is Late Latin materialis, the adjective of materia 'stuff', which passed through Old French into English. Its parent noun is the same source as matter.
intro.cn: material 是晚期拉丁 materialis，即 materia「材料」的形容词，经古法语进入英语；其母名词与 matter 同源。

items.en: Materia meant timber, stuff and subject matter; the adjective materialis was formed on it in later Latin.
items.cn: materia 指木料、材料与题材；形容词 materialis 是晚期拉丁语在它之上构成的。

items.en: Materialis meant 'of matter, physical' and was used in philosophy to contrast the physical with the spiritual.
items.cn: materialis 意为「物质的、物理的」，在哲学中用来与精神相对。

items.en: Old French material brought the adjective and noun into English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 material 在十三、十四世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century material was the ordinary word for cloth in a household, a sense that still survives in tailoring.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，material 已是家庭里指布料的常用词，这一义至今留在裁缝行当。

items.en: Modern law and accounting use 'material' for facts that can shift a decision, an extension of the idea of having real substance.
items.cn: 现代法律与会计用 material 指能改变决定的事实，这是「有实质」这一想法的延伸。

items.en: First recorded dates for the cloth, legal and accounting senses are approximate; the core adjective is well attested from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 布料义、法律义与会计义的最早记录年代为约数；核心形容词义在十四世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds near-forms of material, some sharing its Latin stock and some not; the second group holds words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 material 形近的词，有的同出拉丁词源，有的不是；第二组是词义部分重叠的词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb built directly on materia; material is its learned adjective, so the two share a root but not a part of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 materia 构成的名词与动词；material 是它的书面形容词，二者同根而词性不同。

entries.definition: The same word borrowed a second time from French and narrowed to military stores; it is not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词第二次从法语借入，收窄为军用物资；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: From mater 'mother', not materia; any family resemblance rests on the unproven mater-materia hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mater「母亲」而非 materia；所谓亲缘只建立在那条未获证实的假说上。

entries.definition: The adverb of material, used for 'to a significant degree'; it is a derived form, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: material 的副词，表示「达到显著程度」；它是派生形式，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: Material seen as the thing that underlies qualities; substance is more abstract and less countable.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作承载属性的材料；substance 更抽象、更不可数。

entries.definition: Cloth made by weaving; it covers only the textile sense of material.
entries.definitionCN: 织成的布；只覆盖 material 的织物义。

entries.definition: One of the substances combined in a mixture; material is the broader word for what anything is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中的一种成分；material 是更宽泛的「造物之料」。

entries.definition: Facts that support a conclusion; it overlaps the legal sense of material but not the sense of source material.
entries.definitionCN: 支持结论的事实；与 material 的法律义部分重叠，但不指写作素材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Materialis is the Latin adjective of materia, so material is literally 'of stuff'.
normal.cn: materialis 是 materia 的拉丁形容词，因此 material 字面上就是「属于材料的」。

normal.en: The family runs material, materially, materiality, materialism and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 material、materially、materiality、materialism 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: raw material, building material, material world.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物质义：原材料、建筑材料、物质世界。

normal.en: In law, a material fact is one that can change the outcome.
normal.cn: 在法律里，具有实质性的关键事实才能改变结果。

normal.en: The same Latin stock gives matter, and material is its adjective.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词源也给出 matter，而 material 是它的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cutting table where the cloth decides what the coat can become.
abstract.cn: 想象一张裁床，布料本身决定了这件外套能做成什么样。

abstract.en: Picture a potter's hands choosing clay before any shape is attempted.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠在动手塑形之前先挑泥料。

abstract.en: Picture a folder of notes that a writer keeps beside the blank page.
abstract.cn: 想象作家把一叠笔记放在空白稿纸旁边。

examples.en: Recycled material now accounts for a third of the plant's input.
examples.cn: 回收材料现在占这家工厂投入的三分之一。

examples.en: The committee judged the omission material to the audit.
examples.cn: 委员会认定这处遗漏对审计有实质影响。

examples.en: Course material is posted online before each lecture.
examples.cn: 课程材料在每次讲课前发布到网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买铁料」——盖房装修先买铁、买料，买的都是材料 → 材料、原料

root: 拉丁 materia「材料、木料」→ 晚期拉丁 materialis（materia 加形容词后缀）「物质的」→ 古法语 material → 英语 material；「布料」「重要」义由「做成东西的料」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat something as the stuff a thing is made from: bricks for a bridge, cloth for a coat, notes for a story, supplies for a term, the physical world for the spirit, facts for a decision, money for a life, and a person for a post.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物当作「造物之料」：桥的砖、外套的布、报道的笔记、学期的用品、对抗精神的物质世界、影响决定的实据、支撑生活的钱财，以及适合某职位的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth on a cutting table, waiting to become something else.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁床上的一匹布，等着被做成别的什么。

branches.en: THE STOCK ITSELF: raw stuff in bulk, and the same stuff counted out as supplies for a term.
branches.cn: 原料本身：成批的生料，以及按学期点清的同一种用品。

branches.en: THE CLOTH ON THE TABLE: the material a household handles most often is fabric.
branches.cn: 桌上的那匹布：家庭最常打交道的材料就是织物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL OF A TEXT: notes and sources are clay for a writer's pot.
branches.cn: 文本的料：笔记与来源是作家制陶的黏土。

branches.en: THE TOUCHABLE WORLD AND ITS GAINS: what can be touched, and what can be accumulated from it.
branches.cn: 可触摸的世界及其收获：摸得着的那一面，以及从那一面攒下的东西。

branches.en: STUFF THAT DECIDES: a fact with substance changes a contract, and a person with substance fills a post.
branches.cn: 起决定作用的料：有实质的事实能改动合同，有实质的人能补上职位。

intro.en: Material is one Latin root plus one adjective suffix, and both parts recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: material 由一个拉丁词根加一个形容词后缀构成，这两部分在英语的一大批词里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia gives matter and material; the suffix -alis, through French -al, also shapes manual, editorial and commercial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 也构成 manual、editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of stuff.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把「材料」变成形容词。

items.example: Material carries both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有物质与重要两义。

items.exampleCN: 同一词尾出现在 manual 与 editorial 中。

items.exampleCN: 审计师先判断重要性，再核对数字。

items.meaning: the belief that matter is all there is
items.meaningCN: 认为物质即一切的学说
items.example: The suffix turns a quality into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把一种性质变成一种主义。

items.example: The design materialized as a real bridge.
items.exampleCN: 设计落实成了一座真实的桥。

items.example: The prefix denies both the stuff and the weight.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「实体」与「分量」。

items.example: A second borrowing narrowed to army stores.
items.exampleCN: 第二次借入的形收窄为军队物资。

definition_en: every person; all people

senses.title: Every person, all people
senses.definition: every single person in a group, taken together but followed by a singular verb
senses.definitionCN: 一群中的每一个，整体看待但后接单数动词
senses.example: Everyone in the class passed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 班里每个人都通过了考试。
senses.why: Built on every, the word ticks every name on the list, then counts the ticks as one whole.
senses.whyCN: 由 every 构成的这个词先逐个点名单，再把勾作为一个整体统计。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: people in general, often in common sayings like everyone knows
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一般人，常见于 everyone knows 等俗语
senses.example: Everyone knows the school bell rings at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都知道学校的铃八点响。
senses.why: When no particular group is named, the roll call stretches to the whole community.
senses.whyCN: 当未指明具体群体时，点名册扩展到整个群体。

intro.en: Everyone is the fusion of every and one. The word keeps its singular grammar even though it speaks of many.
intro.cn: everyone 由 every 与 one 融合而成。虽指多人，语法上保持单数。

items.en: The roots aefre (ever) and aelc (each) waited in Old English before the fusion.
items.cn: 古英语中 aefre（ever）与 aelc（each）在融合之前已并存。

items.en: The fused every appeared in the thirteenth century, ready to join with one.
items.cn: 十三世纪融合词 every 出现，为与 one 结合做好准备。

items.en: Everyone was formed as a pronoun, sharing work with the older everybody.
items.cn: everyone 构成代词，与更早的 everybody 分担功能。

items.en: Grammar books settled the singular verb: everyone is, not everyone are.
items.cn: 语法书确定单数动词：everyone is 而非 everyone are。

items.en: The plural their, as in everyone brought their book, is now widely accepted.
items.cn: 复数 their（如 everyone brought their book）如今已被广泛接受。

note.en: The first group collects the every-compound family; the second collects near meanings about people as a whole.
note.cn: 第一组收集 every 复合词族；第二组收集与「全体的人」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: the same meaning, a friendlier spoken tone
entries.definitionCN: 人人。意义相同，语气更口语亲切。

entries.definition: every thing, not every person; objects and facts
entries.definitionCN: 每件事；一切。指物不指人。

entries.definition: in every place, an adverb of location
entries.definitionCN: 到处。地点副词，与人物无关。

entries.definition: the whole group, takes plural verbs

entries.definition: one by one, a more careful counting view
entries.definitionCN: 每个人（逐个）。强调逐个视角。

entries.definition: any person at all, often in questions and negatives
entries.definitionCN: 任何人。常用于疑问句与否定句。

normalIntro.cn: 五条基于语法事实与课堂用语的具体联想。

normal.en: Say hello to everyone opens many a class naturally.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a class photo with no missing face.

senses.title: Grain plants or their seeds

definition_en: the vast body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the earth
core_image: 一整片连成一体的咸水把陆地围在中间，望不到对岸，也数不清有多少层浪
scene: 地理课上，老师转动地球仪，指着连成一片的蓝色说， A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean 指「地球上环绕陆地的巨大咸水体」（第 1 个义项：连成整体、覆盖大部分地表的咸水）；句意为：一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地；对应第 1 个义项。
