senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，深海」——看到望不到边的水，先「哦」一声，再想到深海大洋 → 海洋、大量

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

items.meaning: the stream believed to encircle the world
items.meaningCN: 古人想象中环绕世界的大河
items.example: Homer places Okeanos at the rim of the known world.
items.exampleCN: 荷马把 Okeanos 放在已知世界的边缘。

items.structure: Okeanos → Latin Oceanus → Old French occean
items.example: The ocean covers most of the planet.
items.exampleCN: 海洋覆盖了地球的大部分。

items.meaning: the scientific description of the sea
items.meaningCN: 对海洋的科学描述与研究
items.example: Oceanography combines chemistry, physics and biology.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学结合了化学、物理学与生物学。

items.meaning: a person who studies the sea
items.example: The oceanographer lowered a probe to the trench floor.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学家把探测器下放到海沟底部。

items.meaning: a large enclosure for living sea animals
items.meaningCN: 饲养活体海洋动物的大型场馆
items.example: The oceanarium rebuilt its reef tank.
items.exampleCN: 这座海洋馆重建了珊瑚礁展缸。

items.example: Oceanfront lots sold out within a week.

items.meaning: built for crossing the open sea
items.example: The yard launched an ocean-going tug.
items.exampleCN: 船厂下水了一艘远洋拖船。

items.meaning: the island region of the Pacific
items.exampleCN: 大洋洲包含成千上万座岛屿。

latinEntries.meaning: the great outer sea; also its divine name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 外围的大海；亦为海神之名

latinEntries.structure: oceanicus, oceanica, oceanicum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 日期；日子；约会；枣；注明日期
definition_en: a day of the month or year; an appointment; a sweet fruit; to write the date
core_image: 日历上被圈出的那个格子
scene: 发试卷时老师提醒大家先写名字和考试日。 Please write your name and the date at the top of the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 date 是「日期」（第 1 个义项：某月某日）；句意是请在试卷顶端写上姓名和日期。

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加 date 构成，义为「更新；使现代化」
date 的过去分词转形容词，义为「过时的；注有日期的」

senses.title: A day of the month or year
senses.definition: a numbered day of a month, often written on papers and diaries
senses.definitionCN: 某月中的某一天，常写在文件和日记上
senses.example: The exam date is written on the notice board.
senses.exampleCN: 考试日期写在通知栏上。
senses.why: Calendars cut time into squares, and each square needs its own label.
senses.whyCN: 日历把时间切成格子，每个格子都需要一个标签。

senses.title: An appointment, especially romantic
senses.definition: a planned meeting with someone, especially a romantic one
senses.definitionCN: 事先约好的会面，尤指恋人间的
senses.example: They watched a film on their first date.
senses.exampleCN: 他们第一次约会看了一场电影。
senses.why: A fixed meeting shares the fixed square of time, so the appointment borrowed the calendar word.
senses.whyCN: 定好的会面占用固定的时刻，于是约会借用了日历的词。

senses.title: A sweet brown fruit
senses.definition: a sweet sticky brown fruit from a palm tree
senses.definitionCN: 棕榈树结出的甜而黏的褐色果实
senses.example: We ate dates and nuts at the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间我们吃了椰枣和坚果。
senses.why: A homonym from Arabic: the fruit came with its own word and landed on the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这是来自阿拉伯语的同形异源词：果实带着自己的词，碰巧与「日期」同形。

senses.title: To write or fix the time
senses.definition: to write the day on something, or to say how old something is
senses.definitionCN: 在某物上写日期，或判断某物的年代
senses.example: The bridge dates back to the Qing dynasty.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的历史可以追溯到清代。
senses.why: Papers must carry their time square, so the verb stamps it on.
senses.whyCN: 文书必须携带自己的时间坐标，动词便把这个坐标「盖」上去。

items.en: datum meant given, the past participle of dare, to give; letters were marked datum, given (at this place and time).

items.en: English took the time sense in the fourteenth century; the fruit sense arrived a century later.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪吸收时间义；果实义晚一个世纪传入。

items.en: Modern use adds dating events, out of date and digital dates on files.

definition_zh: 沉重地；猛烈地；大量地
definition_en: in a heavy way; with force or in large amounts
core_image: 大雨砸在屋顶上的声音：密集、用力、不停歇
scene: 窗外雷声滚滚，雨点噼里啪啦往下砸。 It rained heavily all night long.
sceneCN: 这里 heavily 是「猛烈地、大量地」（第 1 个义项：以沉重剧烈的方式）；雨整夜下得又大又急，heavily 描述雨的强度。

derivatives.zh: 重的；猛烈的，heavily 的基础形容词
沉重；沉重感，由 heavy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成
举起；拉起，同族词，指用力搬动

senses.title: With great weight or force
senses.definition: with a lot of weight, force, or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的重量、力量或强度
senses.example: Snow fell heavily on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 雪大量落在山路上。
senses.why: Heavy things press down hard, so doing something heavily means doing it with full force.
senses.whyCN: 重物向下压迫，heavily 做副词即表示以全力或高强度行事。

senses.title: In large amounts or degrees
senses.definition: in large quantities or to a great degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量大或程度深
senses.example: The city relies heavily on tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市严重依赖旅游业。
senses.why: Weight also measures amount: what presses down in quantity presses down in importance too.
senses.whyCN: 重量也衡量数量：数量上的沉重也意味着程度上的深，heavily 由此表示大量与深度。

intro.en: Heavily is the adverb form of heavy, an old English word of weight.
intro.cn: heavily 是 heavy 的副词形式，heavy 是个古老的英语重量词。

items.en: Old English hefig meant having great weight.
items.cn: 古英语 hefig 意为「有很重的分量」。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *habjan, related to the verb have and the idea of lifting.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *habjan，与动词 have 及「举起」的概念相关。

items.en: In Middle English, heavy and hevy varied in spelling as the word spread.
items.cn: 中古英语中 heavy 与 hevy 等拼写并存。

items.en: The adverb heavily formed with the standard suffix -li.
items.cn: 副词 heavily 由标准后缀 -li 构成。

items.en: Modern English extended heavily to rain, breathing, weapons, and dependence.
items.cn: 现代英语把 heavily 扩展到雨、呼吸、武器与依赖。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of heavily.
note.cn: heavily 的形近词与义近词。

normal.cn: 结构「heavy + -ly」：形容词变副词的基本规则。

normal.en: rain heavily
normal.cn: 搭配「rain heavily」（雨下得大）是最常见用法。

normal.en: breathe heavily
normal.cn: 短语「breathe heavily」（沉重呼吸）锁定身体义。

normal.en: rely heavily on
normal.cn: 搭配「rely heavily on」（严重依赖）记住程度义。

normal.en: heavy base first
normal.cn: 先记 heavy（重的），副词含义随之而来。

abstract.en: Hear rain hammering the roof without stopping.
abstract.cn: 听雨点不停砸打屋顶：heavily 的节奏就是密集用力。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders sink under a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 感受肩膀被重包压得下沉：沉重感即 heavily 的本源。

abstract.en: See a city map crowded with tourist icons.
abstract.cn: 看见城市地图上挤满旅游图标：依赖 heavily 即占比极高。

examples.en: It snowed heavily, and all the schools closed.
examples.cn: 雪下得很大，所有学校都停课了。

examples.en: After the race, he lay on the grass breathing heavily.
examples.cn: 赛跑结束后，他躺在草地上沉重地呼吸。

examples.en: This region depends heavily on farming for income.
examples.cn: 这个地区的收入严重依赖农业。

definition_zh: 高度；身高；高处
definition_en: how tall someone or something is; the distance from bottom to top
core_image: 从地面到头顶的那条垂直线：一卷从底拉到顶的皮尺
scene: 体检时护士让他脱鞋站直，把皮尺从地面拉到他头顶。 The doctor measured his height against the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 height 是「身高；高度」（第 1 个义项：从底到顶的距离）；皮尺量出的地面到头顶的长度，正是 height 表示高度的用法。

senses.title: The distance from bottom to top
senses.definition: the measurement of how tall a thing or person is
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从底到顶的量度
senses.example: The tree reaches a height of ten meters.
senses.exampleCN: 这棵树高达十米。
senses.why: A ruler dropped from the sky measures the vertical span, and the word names that span.
senses.whyCN: 一把从天而降的皮尺量出垂直跨度，这个词命名的就是这段距离。

senses.title: A place far above the ground
senses.definition: a place or position far above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 远离地面的位置
senses.example: Some birds can fly at great heights.
senses.exampleCN: 有些鸟能在高空飞行。
senses.why: The measured distance becomes a place at that distance, so heights are the far-up spots.
senses.whyCN: 量出的距离变成了位于该距离之处，heights 便是高远之地。

senses.title: The strongest point or degree
senses.definition: the time or level when something is strongest
senses.definitionCN: 事物最强的时刻或程度
senses.example: The storm was at the height of its power.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴正处于最强时刻。
senses.why: The top of a measure becomes the peak of an event, so the tallest point stands for the strongest time.
senses.whyCN: 量度的顶端变成事件的巅峰，最高点由此代表最强时刻。

intro.en: Height comes from high through one of English's strangest spelling journeys.
intro.cn: height 由 high 演变而来，经历了英语中最奇特的拼写旅程之一。

items.en: Old English had hiehthu, built on the adjective heah, meaning high.
items.cn: 古英语作 hiehthu，建立在形容词 heah（高）之上。

items.en: The root *hauhaz meant high across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 *hauhaz 在各日耳曼语言中表示「高」。

items.en: In Middle English, spellings like heighte and heghte competed for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语中 heighte、heghte 等拼写竞争数百年。

items.en: The th ending was influenced by analogy with words like depth and width.
items.cn: th 词尾受 depth、width 等词类推影响。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling height, though the gh stays silent.
items.cn: 现代英语固定拼写为 height，尽管 gh 不发音。

note.en: Look-alikes and measure neighbours of height.
note.cn: height 的形近词与度量近邻。

abstract.en: Look down from a cliff edge and feel the drop.
abstract.cn: 从崖边俯视感受落差：heights 是脚下遥远的距离。

abstract.en: Watch a storm peak at noon and fade.
abstract.cn: 看风暴在正午达到顶点再消退：height 即最强时刻。

examples.en: He felt dizzy looking down from such a height.
examples.cn: 从这么高的地方往下看，他觉得头晕。

definition_zh: 星期；周；一周（工作周）；七天的期间
definition_en: a period of seven days, usually counted from Monday to Sunday, and also the working days in it
core_image: 墙上挂历被撕下七页，边缘参差，露出新的一周
scene: 宿舍墙上挂着一本薄薄的日历，每过一天撕一页，撕下七页就在下面写一行小结。 She tore off a page a day, and every week ended with a line of notes.
sceneCN: 这里 week 是「星期」（第 1 个义项：七天的期间）；句意为她每天撕一页，每周结束时写一行小结。被撕下七页、边缘参差的挂历就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Seven days
senses.definition: a period of seven days, counted from a fixed day or from any day
senses.definitionCN: 从固定一日或任意一日算起的七天
senses.example: The course lasts six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课持续六个星期。
senses.why: This is the basic unit: a run of seven days.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本单位：连续七天。

senses.title: A calendar week
senses.definition: the seven days from Monday to Sunday as marked on a calendar
senses.definitionCN: 日历上从周一到周日的七天
senses.example: The report is due by the end of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在本周末前到期。
senses.why: For schedules people count from Monday, giving the week a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 在日程安排中人们从周一数起，给一周一个固定框架。

senses.title: The working week
senses.definition: the days set aside for work, usually Monday to Friday
senses.definitionCN: 用于工作的那些日子，通常为周一到周五
senses.example: She works a four-day week.
senses.exampleCN: 她一周工作四天。
senses.why: From the seven days the word narrows to the days that count as work.
senses.whyCN: 从七天缩窄到算作工作的那些天。

senses.title: The week as a business period
senses.definition: the period a business or paper treats as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 商家或报刊所算作一个单位的期间
senses.example: This week we have three new offers.
senses.exampleCN: 本周我们有三项新的优惠。
senses.why: Traders cut the continuous cycle into weeks for counting sales and notices.
senses.whyCN: 商家把连续的循环切成周，用来计算销量与公告。

senses.title: Weak in compounds
senses.definition: used in compounds such as weekday, weekend and midweek to place events
senses.definitionCN: 用于 weekday、weekend、midweek 等复合词，标定时间位置
senses.example: Plans change at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末的时候计划会变。
senses.why: Compounds let one word locate any event within the cycle.
senses.whyCN: 复合词让一个词把事情放到循环中的某处。

intro.en: Week is a Germanic word for a period of seven days, replacing an older English word of the same meaning.
intro.cn: week 是日耳曼语中表示七天的词，取代了同义的古英语旧词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant a turn or a series, and was applied to the cycle of days.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为一轮或一系列，被用来指日子的循环。

items.en: Wice named a week, while the older seofonnihte, seven nights, still served in law.
items.cn: wice 指一周，而更古老的 seofonnihte（七夜）在法律中仍在使用。

items.en: Week replaced the older counting form and became the ordinary word.
items.cn: week 取代了旧的计法，成为普通用词。

items.en: Compounds such as weekday and weekend fixed the week’s inner shape.
items.cn: weekday、weekend 等复合词固定了一周内部的形状。

items.en: A four-day week and a working week show the word measuring labour.
items.cn: a four-day week 与 working week 显示这个词可以衡量劳动。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like week, the second names neighbouring spans of time.
note.cn: 第一组与 week 形近音近，第二组是相邻的时间段。

entries.definition: Two weeks, fourteen nights.
entries.definitionCN: 两星期

entries.definition: A period of about thirty days.
entries.definitionCN: 月

entries.definition: A fixed period of study or office.
entries.definitionCN: 学期；任期

entries.definition: Any length of time marked off.
entries.definitionCN: 时期；周期

normalIntro.en: Keep week as seven days first, then let compounds split it into work and rest.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住 week 是七天，再由复合词把它分成劳作与休息。

normal.en: Week is the span; weekday and weekend divide it.
normal.cn: week 是整段，weekday 与 weekend 把它分开。

normal.en: Weekly is the adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: weekly 是形容词也是副词。

normal.en: Do not confuse week with weak.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 weak 混淆。

normal.en: Within a week means before seven days pass.
normal.cn: within a week 意为七天之内。

normal.en: Week by week describes slow, steady change.
normal.cn: week by week 描述缓慢而稳定的变化。

abstract.en: Picture seven torn pages lying in a heap.
abstract.cn: 想七张撕下的纸堆在一起。

abstract.en: Feel the corner of the pad curl as you tear.
abstract.cn: 感受撕页时纸本边角卷起。

abstract.en: See a fresh page appear above the notes.
abstract.cn: 看笔记上方又出现一张新纸。

examples.en: We stayed in the mountains for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里待了一个星期。

examples.en: The shop opens late twice a week.
examples.cn: 这家店每周有两次开得晚。

examples.en: She has a busy week ahead of her.
examples.cn: 她接下来一周很忙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威克」——威克家的挂历一撕七页，就是一周，撕完一圈再从头。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一轮、一系列）→ 古英语 wice（一周）→ 中古英语 week；同源词有 weekday、weekend、weekly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as seven days, narrows to the calendar frame and the working week, then works inside compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从七天出发，缩窄到日历框架与工作周，再在复合词里发挥作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: seven torn calendar pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：七张撕下的日历页。

branches.en: The span branch: a course lasting six weeks.
branches.cn: 长度分支：持续六周的课程。

branches.en: The calendar branch: due by the end of the week.
branches.cn: 日历分支：周末前到期。

branches.en: The work branch: a four-day week and a week of offers.
branches.cn: 工作分支：四天工作周与一周的优惠。

branches.en: The compound branch: plans that change at weekends.
branches.cn: 复合分支：周末变化的计划。

branches.en: The origin branch: a turn of the days.
branches.cn: 起源分支：日子的一轮。

intro.en: Week compounds with day, end and mid to place events, and takes -ly as an adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: week 与 day、end、mid 复合以标定时间，并加 -ly 作形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 乘客；旅客；随行者；旅鸽
definition_en: a person who travels in a vehicle but is not driving or working on it, a person who takes no active part in something, or the extinct migratory pigeon of North America
core_image: 渡轮甲板上挤满拎着行李的人，海风把衣角吹得鼓起
scene: 清晨的渡轮刚离岸，甲板上的人扶着栏杆看城市退远。 Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
sceneCN: 这里的 passenger 是「乘客、旅客」（第 1 个义项：乘坐交通工具的人）；句意为渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。图中可辨识物件：栏杆、行李、海面。

derivatives.zh: 与 passenger 同出古法语 passager（过往的），后受 passage 影响改写词形，义为「航程；一段文字」
这一族词的基础动词，来自拉丁语 passus（一步），义为「经过；通过」
由 passenger 与 mile 复合而成，是运输业统计客运量的单位「客英里」

senses.title: A person travelling in a vehicle
senses.definition: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train, ship or plane and is not the one operating it
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐汽车、公共汽车、火车、轮船或飞机，但不负责驾驶的人
senses.example: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。
senses.why: The word began as the adjective passager, meaning passing or fleeting, and then named the person who makes a passage; a traveller carried by someone else is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是形容词 passager，意为「过往的、短暂的」，随后用来指走完一段行程的人；被人带着走的旅人正是这个意思。

senses.title: Someone who takes no active part
senses.definition: a person who is carried along by others and takes no active part or responsibility in what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 被别人带着走、对正在发生的事既不参与也不负责的人
senses.example: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。
senses.why: Since a passenger is the one who sits still while another drives, the word easily shifts from a seat on a bus to a seat in a meeting where someone else steers.
senses.whyCN: 乘客就是别人开车时坐着不动的那个人，所以这个词很容易从公交车上的座位，挪到由别人掌舵的会议里的座位。

senses.title: The extinct North American migratory pigeon
senses.definition: a gregarious pigeon of North America that migrated in huge flocks and became extinct in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 一种成群迁徙的北美鸽子，在二十世纪初灭绝
senses.example: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。
senses.why: The bird was named for its habit of passing through in vast migrating flocks, so the same idea of passing travellers gave the species its English name.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，于是「过往的旅人」这同一个想法，给了这个物种它的英文名。

intro.en: Passenger derives from Old French passager, a traveller and also an adjective meaning passing, and its modern spelling was reshaped under the influence of passage.
intro.cn: passenger 源自古法语 passager，既指旅人，也是意为「过往的」的形容词；现代拼写是在 passage 的影响下改成这样的。

items.en: Passus, a step, and the verb passare, to cross, stand at the head of the family.
items.cn: passus（一步）与动词 passare（穿过）位于这一族词的最上游。

items.en: Old French passager meant both a traveller and something passing or brief.
items.cn: 古法语 passager 既指旅人，也指过往的、短暂的事物。

items.en: English took the word as passager, a person who makes a passage or a journey.
items.cn: 英语把它收作 passager，指走完一段行程或旅程的人。

items.en: The spelling gained an n, probably by association with passage, and became passenger.
items.cn: 拼写多出一个 n，可能是因为受了 passage 的类推，于是写成 passenger。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of a person who takes no part, and keeps the name of the extinct passenger pigeon.
items.cn: 现代英语加上「不参与其中的人」这一比喻义，并保留了已灭绝的旅鸽之名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pass or merely spelled alike; the near-meaning group collects words for people who travel.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 pass 之上或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示出行者的词。

entries.definition: To go past something, or a permit to travel.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某物，或通行证。

entries.definition: A way through, a journey, or a part of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 通道、航程，或文本的一段。

entries.definition: An official document that lets you travel abroad; the second element is port, not a form of pass.
entries.definitionCN: 准许出国的官方证件；后半部分是 port，并非 pass 的变形。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling or enthusiasm; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感或爱好；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person who is making a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 正在旅行的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels regularly between home and work.
entries.definitionCN: 定期往返于家与工作地点之间的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels on a horse, bicycle or bus.
entries.definitionCN: 骑马、骑车或乘车的人。

entries.definition: A paying passenger, or the money paid for a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱的乘客，或所付的车费。

normalIntro.en: Passenger is a traveller word that has been reshaped by the word for the trip, so its hooks follow the person being carried rather than the driving.
normalIntro.cn: passenger 是一个表示旅人的词，被「行程」这个词改过形，所以记忆钩子跟着「被带着走的人」，而不是开车的人。

normal.en: Passenger comes from Old French passager, a traveller, and the extra n came later under the influence of passage.
normal.cn: passenger 来自古法语 passager（旅人），多出来的 n 是后来受 passage 影响才加上的。

normal.en: The opposite of a passenger is the driver: one is carried, the other does the carrying.
normal.cn: 乘客的对立面是司机：一个被带着走，一个负责带人走。

normal.en: Passenger seat is the seat beside the driver, named from the person who usually sits there.
normal.cn: passenger seat 是司机旁边的座位，因常坐在那里的人而得名。

normal.en: The passenger pigeon was named for passing through in huge migrating flocks, not for carrying anyone.
normal.cn: 旅鸽因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，并不是因为它载过谁。

normal.en: Passport looks related but its second half is port, a harbour, so the two words only share a beginning.
normal.cn: passport 看起来相关，但它的后半部分是 port（港口），两个词只是开头相同。

abstract.en: A passenger is proof that progress is often made by someone else, which is why the word can sound grateful or helpless.
abstract.cn: 乘客的存在说明前进常常是别人完成的，所以这个词听起来既可能带着感激，也可能带着无力。

abstract.en: Being called a passenger in your own life is a quiet complaint: the vehicle moves, but your hands are not on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 在自己的人生里被叫作乘客，是一句安静的抱怨：车在走，但方向盘不在你手上。

abstract.en: A bird named after passing shows that a whole species can be remembered by one habit of movement.
abstract.cn: 一种因「过境」而得名的鸟说明：整个物种可以被一个移动的习惯记住。

examples.en: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
examples.cn: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。

examples.en: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。

examples.en: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
examples.cn: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派森杰」——派森杰拎着箱子挤上渡轮，找到座位就交给船夫去开；记住 passenger 是乘客。

root: 来自古法语 passager（旅人，也指「过往的」），其词根为拉丁语 passus（一步）与 passare（穿过）；现代拼写受 passage 影响加入 n，并非另有一个新词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person carried along by someone else's movement; the senses divide into the traveller, the figure who takes no part, and the bird that passes in flocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被别人的移动带着走的人；义项按「旅人」「不参与其中的人」「成群过境的鸟」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ferry deck crowded with people holding luggage, the wind filling their coats.
core.cn: 核心意象：渡轮甲板上挤满拎着行李的人，海风把衣角吹得鼓起。

branches.en: a deck crowded with coats and bags
branches.cn: 挤满外套与行李的甲板

branches.en: a ticket checked at the gangway
branches.cn: 在舷梯口被查验的一张票

branches.en: a meeting where one person only listens
branches.cn: 一个人只带耳朵的一场会议

branches.en: a car moving while the hands stay still
branches.cn: 双手不动而车在前进

branches.en: a sky darkened by a migrating flock
branches.cn: 被迁徙鸟群遮暗的天空

intro.en: The word is a French traveller noun built on the Latin step, reshaped by the noun for the crossing, so its parts still say a person on a journey.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「一步」之上的法语旅人名词，又被表示「渡海」的名词改过形，各部分至今仍在说「在旅途中的人」。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and passare are recorded, and the French forms descend from them, so the ancestry is reliable up to the spelling change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 passare 均有记录，法语形式由它们而来，因此直到拼写变化之前，世系都是可靠的。

items.meaning: a person carried in a vehicle

items.meaningCN: 护照；后半为 port（港口），与 passenger 只是开头相同
